hal. 01
Executive verdict

Not ready for signature or funds transfer without cures

Based on the supplied screenshots, the opportunity is not rejected outright, but it is not clean enough for deposit, signing, renovation spend, operational launch, or assignment to a third party. The main issue is not the BPN title check itself; it is the gap between the land owner shown by BPN, the person signing the lease, the apparent agricultural/RDTR context, and the incomplete commercial lease drafting.

Overall status
Hold / cure first
Proceed only after authority, zoning, PBG/SLF, tax, and contract fixes.
Primary legal risk
Authority to lease
BPN owner is Pura Puseh Desa Adat Munggu; lease signatory appears individual.
Primary business risk
Use/zoning mismatch
BPN says sawah; RDTR screenshot appears agricultural/food-crop zoning.
Immediate instruction

No payment of the IDR 5,000,000 deposit, no lease signing, no renovation, no public business launch, and no reliance on the lease term until the items marked HIGH below are cured with original documents and PPAT/legal confirmation.

Risk register
hal. 02
Core findings

Red flags that must be cured before proceeding

Risk Finding Why it matters Required cure
HIGH Owner/signatory mismatch BPN shows the owner as Pura Puseh Desa Adat Munggu. The lease signature page shows I Made Suwinda, S.Pd. as First Party. The screenshots do not prove he can bind the Pura/Desa Adat landowner. Formal authority chain: Pura/Desa Adat resolution, appointment letter, power of attorney, KTP/NPWP, and PPAT confirmation that the signatory can grant a 10-year commercial lease.
HIGH Zoning/use uncertainty The title check describes the land condition as "sebidang tanah sawah". The RDTR screenshot appears to place the parcel in agricultural/food-crop zoning. A shophouse or commercial tenant use may need specific confirmation. Official KRK/PKKPR/RDTR printout for the exact NIB/NOP and written confirmation that the planned business use is allowed.
HIGH Building legality missing The file contains no PBG/legacy IMB, SLF, building tax detail, or certificate of lawful use for the two shopouse units. Request PBG/IMB, SLF if applicable, as-built drawings, use/function approval, utility legality, and any renovation permits.
HIGH Lease object not tied to title The lease refers to two shopouse units and 60 m2 rear land, but does not attach a surveyed plot plan showing exactly where those units sit within the 935 m2 certificate or the PBB objects. Attach a signed site plan with boundaries, measurements, access, parking, shared utilities, and rear-land allocation.
MEDIUM Payment schedule ambiguity The text says IDR 240m/year for shopouses plus IDR 20m/year for land with 7% increase, but installment amounts imply 7% increases by multi-year payment blocks, not every year. Rewrite Article 3 with a dated payment table, exact period covered by each payment, late fee, tax treatment, and whether 7% is annual or per installment block.
MEDIUM Template blanks and dispute forum Opening party data and the District Court city appear incomplete in the template. This can create avoidable enforceability and jurisdiction issues. Complete all party identity fields, addresses, ID numbers, governing language, notice addresses, and exact District Court.
MEDIUM Assignment/sublease restriction Article 5 prohibits assignment/sublease without written First Party consent. This can block resale of the business, brand transfer, nominee use, or operating partner changes. Add controlled assignment clause, affiliate/operator consent mechanics, and landlord consent not to be unreasonably withheld.
MEDIUM No detailed operational rights The lease only says lawful business use. It does not specify signage, alcohol, food service, noise, hours, parking, renovations, waste, banjar/community approvals, or license cooperation. Add permitted-use schedule and landlord cooperation obligations for NIB/OSS, business permits, signage, utilities, and community approvals.
02
Commercial math issue in Article 3

The rent base is IDR 240,000,000/year for the shopouses plus IDR 20,000,000/year for the rear land, total IDR 260,000,000/year. The contract payment table totals IDR 2,943,156,000. If the phrase "7% increase" means annual compound escalation for each year of a 10-year term, the total would be approx. IDR 3,592,276,470 - a difference of approx. IDR 649,120,470. If the parties intend escalation only at payment-block dates, the clause must say that explicitly.

Contract stage Date shown Amount shown Comment
Stage I 1 Mar 2026 IDR 260,000,000 Matches first-year combined rent.
Stage II 1 Mar 2027 IDR 834,600,000 Equals 3 x IDR 278,200,000, suggesting a 7% block increase.
Stage III 1 Mar 2030 IDR 893,022,000 Equals 3 x IDR 297,674,000, again block-based, not annual compounding.
Final payment 1 Mar 2033 IDR 955,534,000 Approx. 3 x IDR 318,511,000. Needs exact rounding rule.

03
Document request list
  • Original complete lease PDF/Word, not screenshots, with all Indonesian and English text visible.
  • KTP/ID, NPWP, address, and legal capacity for all signatories.
  • Pura Puseh Desa Adat Munggu authority package: internal approval, appointment letter, power of attorney, and confirmation that the land can be leased commercially for 10 years.
  • Fresh PPAT BPN title check for SHM 22030509.1.03453 and NIB 22030509.02627, dated immediately before signing.
  • Official site plan tying the two shopouse units and 60 m2 rear land to the certificate, PBB objects, access, parking, utilities, and boundaries.
  • Official RDTR/KRK/PKKPR confirmation for the intended business use at the exact location.
  • PBG or legacy IMB, SLF if required, building drawings, utility legality, and any renovation permits.
  • Latest SPPT PBB and STTS/payment receipts for all relevant NOPs, plus arrears clearance.
  • Banjar/Desa Adat or community consent/fees if required for the intended operation.
  • Business licensing pathway: NIB/OSS KBLI, location permit fit, signage, food/alcohol/music/noise permissions if relevant.

Bottom line for Paco Pak

This can become a workable lease only if the owner authority chain, zoning/use permission, building legality, PBB reconciliation, and contract economics are fixed in writing. Without those cures, the client risks paying for a lease that is hard to enforce, hard to license, hard to assign, and potentially exposed to operational shutdown or landlord/community dispute.
